source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Flexential Atlanta - Norcross publishes 1.8 MW of IT capacity across 32,740 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, 1.8 MW supports roughly 180 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same 1.8 MW supports roughly 45 racks. Those figures are assumptions based on density estimates, not operator claims. The floor area is large relative to the power figure, which implies either low average rack density or significant white space, neither of which is confirmed by published data.

The six certifications, SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 for audited controls over financial and operational reporting, PCI DSS for payment card data environments, ISO 27001 for information security management systems, HITRUST for healthcare information, and SSAE 18 as the attestation standard underlying the SOC reports, collectively qualify this facility to host regulated workloads across financial services, healthcare, and retail verticals. Which tenants occupy the facility is not published.

Among the 33 facilities this site has mapped in Georgia, only four publish a megawatt figure, and their combined published capacity is 66.3 MW. This campus ranks fourth among those four by published IT capacity, contributing 1.8 of 66.3 MW, or roughly 2.7 percent of the state's published total. At that scale, this campus is a compliance-oriented colocation site rather than a meaningful node for large-scale AI compute; the power envelope is too small to support significant GPU cluster deployments without a published expansion plan, and no such plan appears in the data.
